channel.title: Lapland.blog · Field journal from Finnish Lapland
channel.description: A first-person field journal from Finnish Lapland: honest, seasonal, written by someone who actually lives here. Aurora, cabins, seasons, food, people.

item.title: Seven and a half minutes a day: how fast autumn daylight fades in Lapland
item.description: In late August Rovaniemi loses about 7.5 minutes of daylight a day and Utsjoki nearly 9. The numbers, the reason and how to plan around them.
item.author: info@laplandvibes.com (The Field Journal)

item.title: 154 Finnish rest areas lose maintenance or firewood: the Lapland list
item.description: Metsähallitus ended maintenance or firewood at 154 rest areas across Finland in 2026. The Lapland sites, and what is planned for 2027.
item.author: info@laplandvibes.com (The Field Journal)

item.title: Packing for Lapland in July: a checklist and the reasons behind it
item.description: July in Lapland brings warm afternoons, cool nights and rain on about half the days. A checklist built on weather statistics and park advice.
item.author: info@laplandvibes.com (The Field Journal)

item.title: Wood-fired sauna at a Lapland cabin: how to heat it, step by step
item.description: How to light and tend a wood-burning sauna stove, when to close the damper and how to cool off in the lake safely, based on Finnish safety advice.
item.author: info@laplandvibes.com (The Field Journal)

item.title: Rovaniemi market square in summer: where it is and what is in season
item.description: The Rovaniemi market square is at Lapinkävijäntie 7 in the city centre. What is in season in July, and where to check the summer events.
item.author: info@laplandvibes.com (The Field Journal)

item.title: Night hiking at Kiilopää in July: trails, light and safety
item.description: In July the night stays light at Kiilopää. Marked trails of 1 to 14 km start at the Kiilopää gate. How to plan a safe night hike there.
item.author: info@laplandvibes.com (The Field Journal)

item.title: Sodankylä's midnight sun: when it shines and how to sleep
item.description: In Sodankylä the sun stays above the horizon from the end of May to mid-July. When the midnight sun shines, how low the sun gets and how to sleep.
item.author: info@laplandvibes.com (The Field Journal)

item.title: Polar night in Rovaniemi: how dark it really gets and what helps
item.description: In Rovaniemi the sun rises every day, even in December, if only for about two hours. How dark the polar night gets, and what helps you through it.
item.author: info@laplandvibes.com (The Field Journal)

item.title: Salmon soup in Rovaniemi: where to get it and what it costs
item.description: Four Rovaniemi restaurants list salmon soup on their own menus, from 14 to 24.20 euros. Prices read on 5 November 2026.
item.author: info@laplandvibes.com (The Field Journal)

item.title: Winter cabin in Lapland: heating, water, power and what to pack
item.description: A Lapland winter cabin can have every comfort or a wood stove and a well. What to check before booking, how to heat safely and what to pack.
item.author: info@laplandvibes.com (The Field Journal)

item.title: How to read an aurora forecast: Kp, solar wind, Bz and clouds
item.description: An aurora forecast has four parts: Kp days ahead, solar wind an hour ahead, magnetometers now, and the clouds. Where to find each and how to read it.
item.author: info@laplandvibes.com (The Field Journal)

item.title: Northern lights in Kemi: where to watch, light pollution and sea ice
item.description: Kemi's open sea lies to the south and west, while the aurora usually appears in the north. Where to watch, and why the sea ice can wait for daylight.
item.author: info@laplandvibes.com (The Field Journal)
